verdict: Snowflake closed its fiscal year with revenue up 30% to $1.28B and $782M of adjusted free cash flow — but heavy share-based pay kept the GAAP result a $310M net loss.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers paying to store and analyze data on Snowflake's platform, billed mostly by usage. Up 30% YoY.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Consulting and training that helps customers get running on the platform. Up 32% YoY.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 27% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 4% YoY.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Down 1% YoY.

follow100Note: Running costs took $91.56 of every $100 of revenue — share-based pay to staff is a large part of Snowflake's GAAP expenses.
otherDetail: Other income of $16M net was $42M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, minus $2M of interest expense and $24M of other expense, net.
footerNote: Snowflake's fiscal year ends Jan 31, so this is Q4 FY26. Non-GAAP operating income was $139M — the gap to GAAP is mostly share-based pay.

takeaways.title: Product growth held at 30%
takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 30% to $1,227M and total revenue to $1,284M. Remaining performance obligations — work customers have committed to — jumped 42% to $9.77B, and net revenue retention was 125%, meaning existing customers spent a quarter more than a year earlier.

takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, by design of pay
takeaways.text: The GAAP net loss was $310M, narrower than $326M a year ago. Snowflake pays staff heavily in shares, which counts as a GAAP expense: on the company's non-GAAP basis, operating income was a profit of $139M.

takeaways.title: Cash flow is the counterweight
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $781M and adjusted free cash flow $782M — 61% of revenue — in the seasonally strong collection quarter. Snowflake added 740 net new customers, up 40% YoY, and 733 customers now spend over $1M a year.
